novelty_flags.label: Theorem 5 (thm:three-latent-depth)
novelty_flags.one_line: Its consumer, “a regression test and benchmark certificate for the general elimination engine,” names neither a published comparator nor an applied domain or open problem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Proceedings landing page, bibliographic record and abstract
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited work exists as the ICML 2025 proceedings paper and studies single-proxy lvLiNGAM identification using higher-order cumulants.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.1, Theorems 3.4–3.6, especially lines 204–245; proof of Theorem 3.6, lines 248–252
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorems 3.4 and 3.5 identify the proxy effect from the first k(ell) cumulants, including the proxy-to-treatment-edge graph; Theorem 3.6 asserts nonidentification at ell=1 through order three via a degree-two elimination relation.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Model specification, lines 89–94; Theorem 5, lines 224–249; Theorem 6, lines 254–279
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes independent non-Gaussian sources with moments through a fixed order and derives higher-cumulant rank constraints and degree-(ell+1) candidate-root polynomials for bivariate effects.

The computer-algebra framework gives generic identification from a linear target polynomial, while a higher-degree target polynomial may or may not imply generic identification; it supplies the relevant elimination machinery.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, Theorem 3.8 and proof locator in Appendix B.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work gives a graph-based full-observational-law characterization of total-effect identifiability in latent-confounded LiNGAM, rather than a finite truncated-cumulant-depth frontier.
The single-proxy paper assumes a known proxy-generating mechanism and a completeness condition, so it is an adjacent but non-subsuming comparator for the unknown-mechanism LiNGAM setting.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Give Theorem 5 a substantive consumer: state how the ell=3 exact result falsifies or certifies a named published k(3)-order workflow, or make it an explicitly scoped validation corollary rather than an independent result.

Publish the complete ell=1 saturated-ideal generators, multiplier certificate, residual for the competing root, and rational atomic charts before presenting the correction to Theorem 3.6 as a headline result.

After the mandatory ell=2,R=3 projection, turn the all-ell OEQ into a conditional formula or a finite algorithm with explicit input encoding, termination bound, and real-feasibility certificate; this would materially strengthen the exact-frontier kernel.

recommended_next_step: Revise the three-latent result’s scientific implication, then advance the exact-depth kernel to Stage 0 with the ell=2,R=3 saturated legal-fiber computation as the first kill test.
